transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because… things have been feeling pretty stuck. I don’t want to make it sound overly dramatic, but I honestly can’t see my studio—or really my life—getting back on track anymore, no matter how hard I work or whatever payment plan they put in front of me. I’m not sure if that’s the right way to explain it.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but most days I wake up and it’s like this heavy, gray feeling is already there. And even when I’m in the shop, around the wood and tools and things I used to really enjoy, it just feels… flat. Sometimes I have to kind of push myself not to just stand there staring. Does that make sense?
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

I’m not really sure how to answer that cleanly. I mean… I still do things, so it’s not like I’ve completely stopped everything. But if you mean whether it feels good the way it used to, I guess… not really. The things I used to look forward to don’t seem to land the same. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

I think… maybe, yeah, but I don’t know if I’d call it completely lost. I still show up for things, still go through the motions. It’s just that the interest isn’t really there the way it used to be. Like I’m doing it because I’m supposed to, not because I’m pulled toward it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been feeling this way?

I guess it’s been… longer than I like to admit. It kind of started after I took on the mortgage for the studio, a little over two years ago. So, maybe about two years and two months now. I don’t know if that’s the kind of timeline you mean.
Have you experienced any periods where these feelings of sadness or emptiness were particularly worse?

Yeah… I think there are stretches where it feels heavier. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days I wake up and it’s like this gray weight is already there before anything’s even happened. And some days in the shop, even around the wood and tools—things I used to really care about—it just feels flat. I’ll catch myself sort of standing there, staring, trying to make myself start. Is that… is that the kind of “worse” you mean?
Would you say these periods where your feelings of sadness or emptiness are particularly worse last for a few days or are they more prolonged?

More prolonged, I think. I mean, it’s not like it just comes for a few days and then really clears up. It’s been kind of there since I took on the studio mortgage… a little over two years ago, about two years and two months now. I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right.
Would you describe your current feelings of sadness or emptiness as mild or moderate?

I’d like to say mild, but… if I’m being honest, it feels more than that. Most days I wake up and that heavy gray feeling is already sitting there. Even in the shop, around the wood and tools I used to really enjoy, everything feels flat, and I have to push myself not to just stand there staring. So… moderate, I guess? Maybe that’s the right word.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

I mean… I still try to. The shop used to be that for me—being around the wood, the tools, working with my hands. And I don’t want to say there’s nothing there at all, because maybe that sounds too strong, but most days I wake up with this heavy gray feeling already on me, and even when I’m in the shop it just feels kind of flat. Sometimes I have to push myself not to just stand there staring.

Does that answer what you mean by enjoying things?
Have you had any thoughts of death or suicide?

I… I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had days where I feel really worn down and kind of wish I could just not have to deal with everything for a while, but I haven’t been making plans or anything like that. I don’t want to worry anyone unnecessarily.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns recently?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I haven’t been keeping close track or anything. I don’t think there’s been some big change that I could point to… maybe some days are off, but I figured that’s normal.

Do you mean like not eating at all, or sleeping way more or less than usual?
Would you say your feelings of sadness or emptiness are interfering with your daily life most of the time?

Yeah… I guess I’d have to say it is, more than I’d like to admit.

I try to keep things going, but I’ve missed bids I should’ve followed up on, and a couple clients who used to call me first have gone somewhere else. Even stupid paperwork—like mortgage stuff—I just let it pile up because I can’t seem to stay on top of the basic parts of running the studio anymore.

And outside of work, I’ve kind of stopped showing up too. I don’t really go to gallery openings, and I haven’t been playing pickup basketball. So… yeah, I’m still functioning, I guess, but barely keeping a foothold in the work and people that used to matter to me.

Is that what you mean by interfering?
Have you had any periods in the last two years where you felt completely unable to experience pleasure?

Completely unable… I’m not sure I’d say completely, exactly. I mean, I can still get through things, and I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

But most days I wake up and it’s like this heavy, gray feeling is already there, sitting on me. And even when I’m in the shop, around the wood and tools—stuff I used to really enjoy—it just feels kind of flat. Sometimes I have to fight not to just stand there staring.

So… maybe not zero pleasure every second, but it’s been pretty close a lot of the time. Does that answer it the right way?
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions on a daily basis?

I’m not sure. I mean, I have off days where I’ll read the same thing a couple times or put off choosing what to do next, but I don’t know if that’s more than normal.

I wouldn’t want to say it’s a daily thing if I’m not sure. What kind of difficulty do you mean—like forgetting things, or just not being able to settle on a decision?
Have you experienced any significant weight loss or gain recently?

I don’t think so… not anything significant, anyway.

My clothes fit about the same, and I haven’t really been tracking the scale. Maybe a few pounds here or there, but nothing I’d point to and say, yeah, that’s a real change. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or emptiness are present nearly every day?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but most days it’s there.

I wake up and it’s like this heavy, gray feeling is already on me. Even when I’m in the shop, around the wood and things I used to really love, it just feels flat. Some days I’m kind of pushing myself not to just stand there and stare.

So yes, I guess I’d say it’s nearly every day. Is that the kind of answer you’re looking for?
Can you tell me more specifically how long these feelings of sadness or emptiness have been present for you, is it more like a few months or has it been over a year?

It’s been… longer than a few months, yeah.

I guess if I’m being specific, it started around when I took on the studio mortgage. That was a little over two years ago now—about two years and a couple months. I kept thinking it was just stress and I’d adjust, but it’s kind of just stayed there. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Would you say these feelings of sadness or emptiness have been consistently present for most of the day?

Yeah… I think most of the day, honestly.

I mean, I can still work and answer customers and do what I’m supposed to do, so it’s not like I’m breaking down all day. But most mornings I wake up and that heavy, gray feeling is already there, and it kind of follows me. Even in the shop, with the wood and the tools and all that, things I used to really enjoy… it just feels flat.

Sometimes I have to push myself not to just stand there staring. So… yes, I’d say it’s there most of the day. Is that okay to say?
